To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IL-3 is both a competence (growth) and a progression (differentiation) factor.
the growth and differentiation requirements of hematopoietic progenitors can be regulated by the phase of the cycle in which the cells reside.
IL-3 can function as both a competence and a progression factor for hematopoiesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which hematopoietic cell growth factors regulate hematopoietic progenitors.
the molecular mechanisms by which hematopoietic cells are regulated by growth factors.
the mechanisms by which growth factor receptor signaling regulates cell cycle progression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ability of hematopoietic CSFs to regulate cell growth and differentiation is a function of the cell cycle stage in which those cells find themselves.
IL-3 can be considered a competence factor for FDC-P1 and FL5.12 cell lines, and G/M-CS F or IL-4 can be considered progression factors for FDC-P cells.
IL-3 acts as a progression and/or competence factor in a variety of hematopoietic cell clones.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cell cycle stage of a cell is a major determinant of the biological response to hematopoietic factors.
hematopoietic cells can be maintained in G0, and that the ability of growth factors to promote cell cycle progression is dependent upon cell cycle stage.
the cell cycle status of a hematopoietic progenitor clone dictates whether it will proliferate in response a particular growth factor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ability of hematopoietic factors to induce cell cycle progression is not only dependent upon the lineage from where the cell is derived, but is also cell cycle stage dependent.
the ability of various hematological growth factors to regulate the cell cycle is dependent not only on lineage, but also on the phase of the cycle.
the ability of various CSFs to regulate cell cycle events is cell cycle stage specific.
